ca_north_face_the.blurb: A secluded granite wall on the flank of Mt. Hoffman in Yosemite's Tuolumne high country, above May Lake. It holds fourteen trad lines, mostly around 5.10, with a few easier ones in the 5.6 to 5.9 range and one low-angle option. The wall sees very few visitors and the rock can be loose, so expect some route-finding and a serious day out rather than a quick roadside session. It faces north, which keeps it cool and out of the sun. The walk in is long, off trail, and involves a steep snowfield, so bring snow-travel skills.
ca_north_face_the.approach: From May Lake, climb the slabs northeast of the summit, then drop into the valley that leads toward the wall and cross a steep snowfield to reach the base. Snow-travel experience is needed.

ca_mccracken_wall.blurb: A single-pitch sport wall on the Owens River Gorge's western flank outside Bishop, directly opposite the Supreme Wizard formation. Its fourteen bolted lines run from 5.8 up to the low 5.12s, with the bulk of them between 5.10 and 5.11. The welded tuff is typical of the gorge. Some lines start from ledges and need a short scramble to get going.

ca_deadman_s_boulders.blurb: A small, quiet bouldering spot in the High Desert at Apple Valley, on a single compact formation not far from the Highway 18 and Bear Valley Road junction. The fourteen problems are mostly very easy, from VB to V2, with just one hard project up around V5. Rock quality is mixed: some lines are sound, others are loose and chossy, so test holds and bring more than one pad because landings are uneven. It suits newer boulderers or a casual stop on the way through, and is not a destination for hard climbing. Mornings and late afternoons in the cooler months are the better times.
ca_deadman_s_boulders.parking_note: A short drive on dirt tracks off Bear Valley Road, just west of the Highway 18 intersection, brings you to the boulders; leave the car close by.

ca_beehive_wall_the.blurb: A compact bouldering wall on Mt. Rubidoux in Riverside, tucked just beneath the Peace Bridge and the summit road. Fourteen problems share roughly 15 feet of coarse but solid rock, from easy warm-ups through the middle V grades up to a single V6. Landings are mostly very good, though a low stone bench at the base of a few problems is worth watching. Many variations are possible, including a long traverse of the whole wall, and it works well for a short session.

ca_h_open_book_area.blurb: A stretch of the sunny south side of Tahquitz Rock above Idyllwild, home to a classic dihedral and the short multi-pitch lines that fan out from it. Of the fourteen climbs, almost all are trad, with a lone bolted line. Grades start at 5.8 and run to the low 5.12s, with most falling between 5.10 and 5.11. The aspect is warm on cool days and gets hot in summer, so shoulder seasons and early starts are the sensible plan. Expect a walk up to the rock and a traverse along its base.

ca_hercules_foot.blurb: A south and southeast facing desert wall in the Middle Earth sector of Fairview Mountain, overlooking the High Desert floor near Apple Valley. Of fourteen routes, ten are bolted sport, a few are trad, and there is one boulder problem. The grades are for climbers past the beginner stage: mostly 5.10, with a handful of 5.11s and 5.12s and one easier line. Expect plenty of sun and wide views; the wall gets hot, so cooler months or early starts are best. Routes are roughly single-pitch height.

ca_hone_pinnacle.blurb: A large, hard-to-miss buttress in the Shooting Gallery section of the Lake Arrowhead Pinnacles in the San Bernardino Mountains. It has fourteen routes, a mix of trad and bolted lines. The range is broad: a few easy 5th-class climbs, several 5.8s and 5.10s, and a handful of 5.11s, so a mixed party can find something. Most routes face south and are well within a rope length, making it a good choice when time is short.
